title: Driver and emergency vehicle operation basics
summary: The habits of a safe apparatus driver: inspecting the vehicle, driving in emergency mode, backing with a spotter, and clearing intersections. Pair it with your department's driving policy and a practical session.
overview: A starter course written by Resgrid in plain language. Your department's driving policy and the law where you drive always come first: add them to each lesson, and pair the course with a practical session on a closed course before anyone drives on the road.

lessons.title: The vehicle inspection
lessons.html:
Inspect the vehicle at the start of every shift and record what you found. A problem found in the bay is far easier to deal with than one found on the way to a call.

  • Walk around the vehicle: tyres, lights, mirrors, compartments and anything leaking.
  • Check the cab: gauges, warning lights, brakes, horn and siren.
  • Take the vehicle out of service and report it when something is not right.

Add your department's inspection checklist.

lessons.title: Know the vehicle
lessons.html:
Every vehicle handles differently. Learn its height, width, weight and how it brakes and turns before you drive it under emergency conditions.

Your department decides who may drive which vehicle and what training and hours they need first.

lessons.title: Arriving safely is the job
lessons.html:
Lights and siren ask other drivers to yield; they do not make them see or hear you. Drive so that you arrive.

  • Everyone on board wears a seatbelt before the vehicle moves.
  • Keep a speed at which you can stop for what you cannot yet see.
  • Expect other drivers to do the unexpected.

Add your department's emergency driving policy here.

lessons.title: Intersections
lessons.html:
Intersections are where emergency vehicles are most often hit. Slow down and be ready to stop on approach.

  • Clear each lane one at a time and make eye contact with other drivers.
  • Come to a complete stop when your department's policy or the law requires it.
  • Never assume that a green light or a siren has cleared the way.

lessons.title: Backing with a spotter
lessons.html:
Use a spotter whenever you back up. Agree on the signals before you start.

  • The spotter stands where the driver can see them in the mirror.
  • If the driver loses sight of the spotter, the driver stops.

lessons.title: Positioning on scene
lessons.html: Where you park protects the crew. Follow your department's positioning policy for roadway incidents and leave room for the vehicles still coming.

questions.text: What should the driver do when they lose sight of the spotter while backing?
questions.explanation: If the driver loses sight of the spotter, the driver stops.
